title: CLAY COUNTY SHERIFF’S REPORT
full_story:
On Thursday morning, the Clay County Sheriff’s Office received a notification from a Community Watch Camera.  The camera had been placed on the property at the request of the owner due to ongoing criminal activity at this location.  Upon the arrival of the sheriff’s office, a deputy located an individual in one of the outbuildings.  The individual was taken into custody without incident.

As a result of this incident Will E. Corry, 25, of Flora, was arrested for Criminal Trespass to Property and Possession of Methamphetamine.  Corry was transported to the Clay County Jail where he is awaiting his first appearance in court.

The charge is merely an accusation, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

title: MITIGATION PLANNING COMMITTEE MEETING
full_story:
The frequency of severe weather events and damages caused by them and other natural hazards will be discussed when the Clay County Hazard Mitigation Planning Committee meets at the Clay County Health Department, in Flora, at 1 pm on Monday, June 22nd.

This Committee, is comprised of County, municipal, healthcare, education, fire protection district, and emergency services representatives, as well as technical partners and stakeholders, will meet over the next several months to update the Clay County Natural Hazards Mitigation Plan.  All Committee meetings are open to the public.

“The goal of this Committee meeting is to identify how often severe weather events occur within the County and what kinds of damages have resulted.  Based on this information the committee will compile lists of activities and projects to reduce damages caused by these events,” said Steve Lewis, Flora-Clay County Emergency Services and Disaster Agency Coordinator.

The focus of this effort is on natural hazards, severe thunderstorms with damaging winds or hail, tornadoes, snow and ice storms, floods, drought, extreme cold, and excessive heat.  Interested persons can provide input at these Planning Committee meetings or submit their comments and questions to their municipal or County representatives.

Participants to date include the County, four municipalities, 10 townships, two school districts, three fire protection districts, the Clay Electric Cooperative, Clay County Water, and Clay County Hospital.  Jurisdictions who have yet to participate in a committee meeting are strongly encouraged to attend this meeting.

“This Plan will be our best resource for determining how to mitigate damages from storms and other natural hazards.  After the Plan is updated, comprehensive information will be available in one document to help guide those who are making decisions about how to better protect residents,” added Lewis.

title: FLEENER STUDENT OF THE MONTH
full_story:
The Illinois Farm Bureau Actively Engaged Student of the Month for June is Ava Fleener.

The recent graduate at North Clay High School is building a lengthy resume.

Fleener gained valuable job experience, working for Wabash Communications, Fat Dad’s Ice Cream Shop and most recently, Knapp Oil and Propane.  But the workforce has not deterred her from being involved in school and community.  In fact, she racked up an impressive 100 hours of community service before graduating.

It’s something that stood out to North Clay FFA Advisor Katrina VanDyke.  “Ava is one of the most well-rounded students that I have had the privilege to work with during my 25 years of teaching,” she said.  “Her time management skills and dedication are second to none.”

Fleener’s roots run deep with 4-H: She is a member of the Little Wabash Deer and Fawn 4-H Club, and has a love of showing Hereford cattle.

“It has always taught me to work hard and it’s a big responsibility,” she said.  “In fact, it’s probably some of the biggest life lessons I have learned.”

Fleener is also deeply committed to FFA and is on track to receive her American FFA Degree in 2027.

“I eventually became an officer with the North Clay FFA and that boosted my FFA experience,” she said.

Interscholastic athletics played a big role in Fleener’s days at North Clay High School, a three-sport athlete competing in volleyball, basketball and softball.

Fleener would also make time for pep club, Spanish club, FCCLA and FCA.

Fleener will attend Olney Central College in the fall with plans to transfer to Eastern Illinois University and major in elementary education.

title: QUILT SHOW
full_story:
The Sew Nifty Sisterhood Quilt Guild is having the “Oh My Stars” America 250 birthday celebration Quilt Show, raffle, and silent auction this weekend.

The show will be at the North Clay Elementary School, in the south building, on Friday from 5 to 7 pm and Saturday, from 9:00 to 4:00 pm.  Admission to the show is $5.00 per person and those 12 and younger get in for free.  There will be a raffle for a “Our flag stands for freedom” quilt with tickets on sale at the door or from any guild member.  There will also be a scavenger hunt and a silent auction.

For more information go to the Sew Nifty Sisterhood Quilt Guild on Facebook.

title: WRECK IN SALEM
full_story:
28-year-old Brock Giddens of Louisville was involved in an accident in Salem Thursday evening.

According to the Salem Police Department Giddens turned east onto West Main in front of the Salem Walmart and collided with an eastbound car driven by 66-year-old Donna Moore of Salem.  Moore was injured and taken to Salem Township Hospital.  Giddens escaped injury.  He was ticketed for failure to reduce speed to avoid an accident.

title: PLUMMER TOWN HALLS
full_story:
State Senator Jason Plummer is set to host two End of Session Town Hall events tonight, to provide residents with an update on recent legislative activity from the 2026 spring session.  The meetings will take place in Olney and in Salem.

The events are free and open to the public.  Residents are encouraged to attend to learn more about actions taken during the spring session, ask questions, and share feedback on issues important to their communities.

In Olney the meeting will be held from 5 to 6 pm at the Olney Public Library.  In Salem the meeting will be held from 7 to 8 pm at the Salem Education Center.  Residents are encouraged to attend, learn more about the spring legislative session, and ask questions about state government.

title: ISP ENFORCEMENT
full_story:
Illinois State Police (ISP) conducted a violent crime suppression detail in St. Clair and Madison counties on Thursday and Friday, focusing its efforts on East St. Louis and neighboring Metro East communities.  The operation utilized intelligence and technology to focus enforcement efforts on known high crime areas, violent offenders, and structured criminal groups in the communities of the Metro East.

The detail resulted in 24 arrests, 40 criminal charges, 26 felony charges, 9 firearms related charges, 8 firearms seized, 287.5 grams of cannabis and 198.5 grams of other controlled substances seized.

ISP officers from around the state, including patrol Troops 3, 6, and 8, ISP Fatal 4 South, Zone 6 Firearms Investigations Unit, Public Safety Enforcement Group (PSEG), Crime Scene Services, ISP SWAT, and ISP Air Operations, assisted ISP Statewide Anti-Violence Enforcement (SAVE) South with this operation.  The Metropolitan Enforcement Group of Southern Illinois provided additional support.  ISP will continue to use all available resources, including air operations, technology, forensic services, investigators, increase patrols, and information sharing to combat violent crime.

title: IGNITE CURIOSITY SUMMER CAMPS
full_story:
Frontier Community College is inviting area students of all ages to explore new interests and develop hands-on skills through its upcoming Ignite Curiosity Summer Camps.  Registration is now underway for the camps which offer creativity and teamwork for a variety of age groups.

Canvas 1 and 2 will be held tomorrow, with Canvas 1 starting at 8 and Canvas 2 starting at 12.  Canvas 1 is an introduction to acrylic painting and Canvas 2 builds on the skills learned in Canvas 1.  The camp is for grades 1 through 8 and cost $35 for each class.  Lego Battle Bots will be held tomorrow at 8 am.  In this hands-on robotics camp students will design, build, and program their own Lego battle bots while learning the basics of robotic coding.  The camp is for those in 3rd through 8th grade and cost $25.  Sign Language Camp will be held on Wednesday starting at 1 pm.  Participants will be introduced to American Sign Language.  The camp is for grades 1 through 8 and cost $25.

To learn more about these camps at FCC or about other camps at the other IECC campuses go to the iecc.edu/communityed website.  To sign up or register for the FCC camps, call or visit the Student Services Office at Frontier Community College.

title: FREE FISHING DAYS
full_story:
Illinois Free Fishing Days start Friday and run through Monday, and the Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) invites families throughout the state to enjoy the opportunity at a lake, pond, river, state park or private fishing hole near them.

During these four days, anglers can fish without purchasing a fishing license, salmon stamp or inland trout stamp in Illinois.  The goal is for those who don’t usually go fishing to discover or rediscover the activity and to introduce children to it.

“Free Fishing Days are a great opportunity for Illinois families to unplug, spend time together outdoors, and discover the fun and enjoyment of fishing,” said IDNR Director Natalie Phelps Finnie.  “Whether you’re new to the activity or simply haven’t been able to find time for it lately, I encourage residents and visitors alike to grab a rod, head to the water, and make fishing an outdoor tradition.”

Outside of Free Fishing Days, Illinois requires anyone over the age of 16 to have a fishing license to fish.  At $15, Illinois has one of the most affordable standard fishing licenses in the Midwest.  Licenses can be purchased at vendors throughout Illinois or online.  Exclusions apply to active-duty military and people with disabilities.

title: FARM BILL COMING
full_story:
The Senate Agriculture Committee is expected to consider a farm bill in July or August, committee chair John Boozman recently told reporters.

Boozman, said the text of the bill will likely be released in the next couple weeks, with consideration taking place during the work period between July 4th and August recesses.  Boozman previously planned to hold a markup of a farm bill by the end of June.

Asked if the bill will include a provision allowing the nationwide, year-round sale of E15, Boozman said he believes E15 should be handled in a standalone bill.

He noted E15 is not in the jurisdiction of the Senate Agriculture Committee.  He also pointed to difficulties the House had advancing a year-round E15 bill, which was ultimately passed by the chamber last month.
